stem: Sarah is an 18-month-old with a two-day fever to 39°C. Urinalysis is positive for nitrites and leukocytes, and the urine is sent for M/C/S. She is otherwise well, drinking adequately, and has normal perfusion. Which ONE of the following would you include in your plan of action?

options.text: Admit for IV ampicillin and gentamicin
Renal ultrasound in next six weeks

explanation: This is a likely urinary tract infection in a clinically stable child who can tolerate oral intake, so oral antibiotics are appropriate. Routine urgent imaging is not indicated for a first uncomplicated UTI in a well 18-month-old.
rationale: The child is haemodynamically stable, appears non-toxic, and is drinking well, so oral treatment is the best immediate management.

optionExplanations.A: IV antibiotics are reserved for children who are unwell, unable to tolerate oral therapy, or have complicated infection.
optionExplanations.B: Urgent renal ultrasound is not required for an uncomplicated first UTI in a stable child.
optionExplanations.C: Appropriate treatment for a well child with UTI who can drink and take oral medication.
optionExplanations.D: Delayed ultrasound is not routinely needed after a straightforward first UTI unless there are atypical features or recurrence.
optionExplanations.E: MCUG is not routinely indicated after a first uncomplicated UTI.

Instructions

There are 7 questions relating to this scenario.

Clinical scenario 2 - Sarah

Sarah, an 18 month old, presents with a two day history of fever to 39°C. She has no history of cough; rhinorrhoea; vomiting; diarrhoea or rash. She attends day care. She has a 5 year old sibling who is at school and is well at the moment. She is eating less than normal but drinking well and passing urine as normal.

On examination she appears slightly flushed with a fever of 38.5°C. Her HR is 110 and RR 28. Her peripheries are warm and her capillary refill time is 1-2 seconds.

She has no rash, no conjunctivitis, her ENT examination is unremarkable. Her heart sounds are dual with no murmur and her chest is clear. Her abdomen is soft and non-tender. Her immunisations are up to date.

The following seven questions refer to Sarah’s clinical scenario.
